title: India goes home empty-handed from the International Emmys as Vir Das and 'Real Kashmir Football Club' lose
dek: France's 'Carême' won best drama and Argentina's 'División Palermo' best comedy in New York. Britain took nine awards; Vijay Sethupathi was a presenter.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Neither of India's two nominees won at the 54th International Emmy Awards in New York on Monday night. The comedian Vir Das's Netflix special "Vir Das: Fool Volume" lost the comedy award to Argentina's "División Palermo – Season 2", and the Sony LIV series "Real Kashmir Football Club" lost best drama series to the French period drama "Carême".

The ceremony, organised by the International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences, was held at the New York Hilton Midtown from 5 pm to 10 pm local time, which was 3.30 am to 8.30 am on Tuesday in India. The American actor Michael Urie hosted. The Tamil actor Vijay Sethupathi was among the presenters, India's only presence on stage.

## The Indian nominees

It was Vir Das's third International Emmy nomination. He won the comedy award in 2023 for "Vir Das: Landing", sharing it with the British series "Derry Girls".

"Real Kashmir Football Club" is a drama inspired by the club founded in Srinagar in 2016, which rose through India's football leagues. Directed by Mahesh Mathai and Rajesh Mapuskar, it stars Manav Kaul and Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub. Kaul had described the nomination as a milestone for the country, according to reports.

India's other big win came in 2020, when "Delhi Crime" won best drama series. At last year's ceremony, the 53rd, the singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh was nominated for best actor and also lost; Britain won the most awards that year too, with seven, and the Disney+ series "Rivals" took best drama.

## The winners

Britain won nine of the evening's awards, according to the published winners list. The main winners were:

- Drama series: "Carême" (France)
- Comedy: "División Palermo – Season 2" (Argentina)
- TV movie or mini-series: "Prisoner 951" (UK)
- Actor: Bobby Schofield, "Unforgivable" (UK)
- Actress: Mona Mina Leon, "Holy Sh!t" (Belgium)
- Documentary: "Louis Theroux: The Settlers" (UK)
- Current affairs: "Exposure: Breaking Ranks: Inside Israel's War" (UK)
- News: "The World: 24 Hours in the Kill Zone", Sky News (UK)
- Arts programming: "Der talentierte Mr. F" (Germany)
- Telenovela: "Leyla" (Türkiye)
- Non-scripted entertainment: "Educating Yorkshire – Season 2" (UK)
- Short-form series: "De Klas van 2000" (Belgium)
- Sports documentary: "The Philipstown Wirecar Grand Prix" (South Africa)
- Kids, animation: "The Scarecrows' Wedding" (UK)
- Kids, factual and entertainment: "Horrible Science" (UK)
- Kids, live action: "Dexter Procter the Ten Year Old Doctor" (UK)

The Founders Award went to Bela Bajaria, Netflix's chief content officer, and the Directorate Award to the Austrian media executive Gerhard Zeiler.

## Why it matters

The International Emmys recognise television made outside the United States, and Indian streaming shows have used nominations to reach audiences abroad. This year's nominations spanned 22 countries, according to reports when they were announced in September; India had two of them.

Closer to home, the International Film Festival of India in Goa continues until 28 November, when its competition awards will be announced.
